label: First Vatican Council, Dei Filius Ch. 1…: The Church believes and confesses one true and living…
locator: ch. 1, unum esse Deum verum et vivum ... intellectu ac voluntate omnique perfectione infinitum: qui cum sit una singularis, simplex omnino et incommutabilis substantia spiritualis
interpretation: The council's confession of God's attributes (DS 3001): one, true, living, creator and lord, almighty, eternal, immense, incomprehensible, infinite in intellect, will and every perfection; one singular, altogether simple and unchangeable spiritual substance; really distinct from the world; most blessed; exalted above all. With 'bonitate sua' (DS 3002) for goodness. Kept as prose. It motivates the intended attribute list of the explicit one-way premise STMT-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-SUFFICE (owner decision on #143, 2026-10-24) and supports the intended readings of the five attribute inputs. The text does not assert a universal bridge over arbitrary predicates or define the skeleton field. As in the root (A), it states what the Church teaches; it is not used as a premise of the derivations.
